replace_in_block.new_heading: What's on a dairy-free catering menu?
new_paragraphs: Plenty, because the trick is starting from cuisines that lean lightly on dairy in the first place. A dairy free menu in Dubai draws on Mediterranean, Levantine, Asian and much of Italian cooking, where olive oil, tahini, coconut and nut-based sauces already do the work butter and cream do elsewhere. Expect dairy-free mains and sauces built from scratch, plant-based milks and cheeses for the dishes that need them, and desserts such as sorbet, coconut panna cotta and olive-oil cake that skip cream entirely. Signature options we build menus around include:
dairy-free mains with reduction and nut- or coconut-based sauces
plant-based milks, butters and cheeses for gratins, bakes and dressings
dairy-free desserts and a sweet table
global favourites adapted, from pasta to curries to mezze
Share any other diets at the table and the chef folds them into one coherent menu instead of a stack of exceptions.

add_block.new_heading: How do you handle a dairy allergy versus lactose intolerance?
new_paragraphs: Carefully, and differently, because the two need different kitchens. Lactose intolerance is about comfort, so a well-built dairy-free menu keeps milk sugars out. A genuine dairy allergy is a safety matter: it means confirming separate prep surfaces, checking every packaged ingredient's label, and avoiding cross-contact throughout service. When you enquire, tell us the severity and we confirm the handling with the business before the event instead of assuming it. This is also where the difference between dairy-free, lactose-free and vegan matters: dairy-free removes all milk-derived ingredients, lactose-free can still contain milk proteins, and vegan removes every animal product. If someone searches "dairy free catering near me" hoping their allergy will be taken seriously, that is exactly the detail we pin down up front.
